entries.title: workshop on “Participatory Models of Higher Education” at Don Bosco Institute, Guwahati

data.body:
Fr. John Paul Tirkey and twelve faculty members from Don Bosco College, Tura attended a workshop on “Participatory Models of Higher Education” at Don Bosco Institute, Guwahati from 13th to 15th July 2026.

The workshop was organized by Don Bosco South Asia for the Provinces of New Delhi, Dimapur, Guwahati and Shillong.

It was an experiential learning program, and the faculty returned with valuable insights for the growth and development of the college.

entries.title: Office and Support Staff Meeting Don Bosco College Tura - 18 February 2026

data.body:
Office and Support Staff Meeting Don Bosco College Tura - 18 February 2026 

A few days after the commencement of the new semester (even), the IQAC and the Management, Don Bosco College Tura convened a meeting of the Office and Support Staff on 18 February 2026 in the Bosco Hall of the college. The first session was led by Dr. Yubaraj Sharma, Assistant Professor and Assistant Coordinator of the IQAC. In his presentation on data management, he emphasised the vital role of systematic documentation and digital record-keeping in advancing NAAC preparations. He highlighted the importance of accurate data collection, organised storage, and efficient retrieval of information at short notice. Dr. Sharma underlined that effective office management today must align with technological advancements, ensuring transparency, speed, and reliability in institutional processes. He encouraged the staff to adopt digital tools proactively and maintain updated records to strengthen the academic and administrative profile of the college. The next session was addressed by Fr. Louis Arimboor, the Administrator. He appreciated the thoughtful initiative of organising the meeting at the beginning of the academic year and commended the office and support staff for their collaborative and dedicated service. He elaborated on administrative responsibilities, stressing that efficiency, teamwork, and clear communication are essential for the smooth functioning of the institution. He expressed satisfaction at the spirit of cooperation among the staff and urged them to continue working with unity and commitment. The final session was conducted by the Principal, who presented a PowerPoint reflection on the core values that guide the institution. He spoke on excellence, confidentiality, accountability, and transparency as foundational principles of effective administration. Emphasising discipline, he reminded the staff that each department must strive to be at its best in order to promote the growth and reputation of the entire institution. He further highlighted the importance of punctuality, cleanliness, honesty, and integrity in daily work, noting that these values build trust and credibility within and outside the college community. The meeting concluded with an interactive session, during which the staff were given the opportunity to ask questions and share suggestions. The discussions were constructive and forward-looking. The gathering ended on a cordial note with a cup of tea, marking a renewed beginning and a shared resolve to serve the institution with greater responsibility and excellence in the new academic year.

entries.title: Civil Society Bodies Engage Don Bosco College Students on Sixth Schedule

data.body:
Civil Society Bodies Engage Don Bosco College Students on Sixth Schedule

On 17 February 2026, Civil Society Organisations of Tura conducted a timely and forward-looking awareness programme for students of Don Bosco College Tura, focusing on the constitutional vision and enduring significance of the Sixth Schedule for the Garo Hills.

Addressing students from the Departments of History and Political Science, Mr Pritam Arengh of the Federation of Khasi Jaintia and Garo People (FKJGP) traced the roots of Garo self-governance — from traditional institutions, to recognition under British rule, and eventual constitutional protection in independent India. He emphasized that the autonomy guaranteed under the Sixth Schedule is inalienable and non-compromisable, firmly embedded in the Constitution of India.

Mr Sengbat Ch Marak of the A'chik Youth Welfare Organisation (AYWO) elaborated on the legal and customary foundations of self-rule, highlighting the delicate balance between customary law and constitutional governance. He cautioned that without robust, transparent, and progressive self-governance, there is a risk of its powers being surreptitiously undermined, as has occurred in the past.

In a stirring address in Garo, Mr Zikku Balgra of the Garo Students' Union (GSU) urged students to equip themselves for ethical and informed leadership, reminding them that the future of the Garo Hills depends on a generation well-versed in constitutional rights and responsibilities.

The interactive session reflected both academic rigor and civic engagement, concluding with a clear and resounding message: autonomy under the Sixth Schedule is not only a constitutional safeguard but also a shared responsibility for future generations.

entries.title: The Combined Annual Training Camp (CATC) was held at the Inter State Bus Terminus (ISBT) campus, Duragre, Tura

data.body:
The Combined Annual Training Camp (CATC) was held at the Inter State Bus Terminus (ISBT) campus, Duragre, Tura, West Garo Hills, Meghalaya, from 7 to 16 February 2026 under the aegis of the 41 Meghalaya Battalion NCC. The camp brought together 550 cadets from across the state, including 60 cadets from the NCC Unit of Don Bosco College, Tura, several of whom appeared for the ‘B’ and ‘C’ Certificate Examinations.

Over the course of ten rigorous days, cadets engaged in intensive training that emphasized discipline, physical fitness, leadership, teamwork, and personality development. Beyond the training drills, they also showcased their individual and collective talents in a variety of competitions. The cadets of Don Bosco College, in particular, shone brightly. Corporal Wema Rimchey R. Marak earned the 1st prize in the Extempore Speech competition for the Senior Wing, while JUO Amit Hajong secured the 1st prize in the Firing competition under the Senior Division, reflecting both skill and focus.

Other cadets also achieved noteworthy success. Sergeant Manmera G. Momin brought home the 3rd prize in Drill Compilation, Cadet Jakchime K. Sangma won 3rd prize in Solo Dance, the Group Song team earned 3rd prize, and Cadet Rapidim Chachura S. Momin was awarded 3rd prize in Solo Song. These achievements highlighted the dedication, teamwork, and talent of the college’s NCC unit.

Earlier, during the Republic Day Celebration on 26 January 2026 at Tura, the NCC Boys’ Unit of Don Bosco College had won 1st prize in the March Past, while the Girls’ Unit claimed 2nd prize, an event graced by Thomas A. Sangma, Hon’ble Speaker of the Meghalaya Legislative Assembly.

Overall, the Combined Annual Training Camp offered an enriching experience that strengthened the cadets’ skills, leadership, and camaraderie. The remarkable accomplishments of the Don Bosco College NCC cadets, from winning competitions to demonstrating discipline and teamwork, stand as a proud testament to their commitment, perseverance, and pursuit of excellence.

entries.title: Parents’ Meeting of II Semester Students (Morning, Day and Evening Shifts)

data.body: The Parents’ Meeting for the II Semester students of the Morning, Day, and Evening shifts was held at 10.30 am in the Bosco Hall of the College. A good number of parents attended the meeting, showing their concern and commitment towards the education of their children. Most of the Morning and Evening shift teachers were present and actively participated in the meeting. The programme began with an introductory address by the Principal, Rev Fr Januarius S Sangma. He stressed the need for greater collaboration between parents and the College for better academic results and the overall growth of students. He reminded everyone that education is a shared responsibility and that when parents and teachers work together, students benefit greatly. The Principal then read a passage from Scripture, played a prayer song for all to listen to, and led the gathering in an opening prayer. After this, he formally welcomed the parents and thanked them sincerely for taking time out of their busy schedules to be present. In his address, the Principal spoke about the Faculty Development Programmes conducted by the College. He explained that these programmes help teachers to improve their teaching methods and remain updated. He highlighted the introduction of Outcome-Based Education (OBE), which focuses on clear learning outcomes and aims to improve the quality of teaching and learning. He expressed hope that this system would help every department and every teacher to guide students more effectively. He then invited the IQAC Coordinator, Dr Meuller Beul M Sangma, to address the parents. She spoke positively about the academic system of the College. She encouraged the parents to motivate the students to take both Major and Minor courses seriously. She explained the mentorship system, where each student is guided by a mentor, and said that this relationship promotes guidance, responsibility, and mutual growth. She also expressed confidence that the Faculty Development Programmes and OBE would further strengthen student performance. She further emphasized the importance of Cognitive, Affective, and Psychomotor skills and highlighted how teachers strive to incorporate these skills into the teaching-learning process, ensuring students develop not just knowledge, but also understanding and practical abilities. This holistic approach will ultimately lead to Outcome-Based Education, equipping students for success. The Principal also spoke openly about certain concerns. He mentioned the difficulty in finding part-time counsellors and stressed the need for better communication between parents and the College. He cautioned against harmful habits such as smoking and drug use, urging parents to guide their children carefully. He emphasised discipline, punctuality, regular attendance, and serious preparation for examinations. He reminded parents that the investment they make in education must bring good academic and personal results. During the question-and-answer session, parents shared helpful suggestions. One important suggestion was to create department-wise WhatsApp groups for better communication. Some parents also mentioned that students do not always share important college information at home. The College assured the parents that efforts would be made to improve communication. Overall, the parents expressed satisfaction with the sincere efforts of the College. The meeting concluded with a photo session. Tea was served to all, and the College Calendar was distributed to the parents. The meeting was meaningful and fruitful. It strengthened the bond between the College and the parents and renewed the shared commitment to guide students towards academic excellence and good character.

entries.title: Saleng encourages students to put God first and never give up on education

data.body:
Saleng encourages students to put God first and never give up on education

TURA, Oct 27 — In his maiden visit to the renowned Don Bosco College, Tura, as Chief Guest for the inauguration of College Week 2025, Shri Saleng A. Sangma, Hon’ble Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha, exhorted students to “put God first,” reminding them that God never fails those who turn to Him in faith and sincerity.

Addressing a packed gathering of students and faculty, the MP urged the youth never to give up on education, calling it the foundation of personal growth and social transformation. “Along with divine help, one must work diligently and persevere to achieve success,” he said, drawing from his own life experiences.

Recounting his student days at Don Bosco, Shri Saleng shared fond memories of his achievements in sports and the encouragement he received from his then Principal, Fr. V. A. Cyriac. He candidly spoke of how the fear of not being able to provide well for his family motivated him to take education seriously. “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom,” he said, inspiring students to blend faith with effort in their pursuit of excellence.

Principal Fr. Januarius Sangma warmly welcomed the MP back to his alma mater, remarking, “Once a Bosconian, always a Bosconian.” He praised today’s Bosconians as young people full of aspirations and lauded the MP as “a leader who goes to the people rather than waiting for the people to come to him.”

Accompanying the MP were Mrs. Ferlina C. A. Sangma, Retd. MCS Officer and former MLA of Selsela, Mr. Benny Roger, Mr. Prewil Ch Marak, and several other dignitaries. The event concluded with a lively cultural programme presented by the students and faculty, showcasing the rich talent and spirit of Don Bosco College, Tura.

entries.title: Understanding Punishment: A Philosophical Exploration of Reformative, Preventive and Retributive Theories

data.body:
Understanding Punishment: A Philosophical Exploration of Reformative, Preventive and Retributive Theories 

On 9th October 2025, the Department of Philosophy, Don Bosco College, Tura organized a departmental seminar for the 5th Semester Honours students on the theme “Understanding Punishment: A Philosophical Exploration of Reformative, Preventive and Retributive Theories”. The seminar was held at 11:00 am in Bosco Hall. The occasion was graced by the Vice Principal of the College, Rev. Fr. John Paul Tirkey, the IQAC Coordinator, Dr. Mueller Buel M Sangma and the faculty members of the Department. A total of 96 participants attended the seminar including Honours students from the first and third semesters, along with the paper presenters from the fifth semester. 

The seminar commenced with a welcome and introductory speech on the theme of the Seminar by the Head of the Department, Dr. Wanphai Mary K. Japang, followed by an address from the IQAC Coordinator, Dr. Meuller Buel M Sangma.  In her speech, Dr. Sangma emphasized the importance of multidisciplinary courses under NEP 2020 and highlighted the close connection between Education and Philosophy. She encouraged students to actively engage in the seminar to enhance their critical understanding and analytical skills.

The seminar was formally inaugurated by the Vice Principal of the College Rev. Fr. John Paul Tirkey. In his address, he shared valuable insights on the philosophical and practical significance of punishment in shaping ethical and moral life. He further motivated students to participate actively in the seminar as such participation would enrich their academic growth and contribute positively to their future endeavours. 

The technical session comprised four group presentations by the fifth semester Honours students, each focusing on different aspects of the theme. The first group explored the concept of punishment from a philosophical perspective, laying the foundation for the discussion. The second group analyzed the "Reformative Theory" which emphasizes that punishment should reform the offenders and guide them toward responsible behavior. The third group discussed the "Preventive Theory" which stresses that punishment aims to prevent future crimes and protect society. The fourth and final group examined the "Retributive Theory" which highlights that punishment ensures justice by giving the offenders what they deserve. Each group effectively presented the concept of punishment, explained the significance of their respective theories and discussed the criticisms offered by various philosophers.  

Jerry Amami R Marak, a fifth semester student, presented a concise summary of the main ideas discussed in each presentation and concluded the technical session by stressing the significance of punishment  in shaping individuals toward ethical and moral behavior.

Following each presentation, participants and paper presenters were encouraged to pose questions to the respective groups. The group representatives and members answered the questions thoughtfully and helped everyone gain a clearer understanding of the seminar theme. 

The seminar was skillfully hosted by Prena Sutradhar from the third semester, who ensured that each session proceeded smoothly.  The Seminar ended with a vote of thanks delivered by Pratima M Marak, a first semester student who expressed sincere gratitude to everyone involved in making the seminar a grand success.

entries.title: Celebration of the National Mathematics Day Cum Inter School Quiz Competition.

data.body:
Celebration of the National Mathematics Day Cum  Inter School Quiz Competition.

 

Host : Department of Mathematics, Don Bosco College, Tura

 Date: 10th October, 2025

 Venue: B.Ed Conference Hall.

 Preamble: 

 A One day programme on Celebration of the National Mathematics Day cum Inter School Quiz Competition has been conducted on 10th October, 2025, at Don Bosco College, Tura in order to spread interest of Mathematics among the students. The National Mathematics Day is actually scheduled on 22nd December to commemorate the Birth Anniversary of the greatest mathematician Srinivas Ramanujan, but as the college remains closed on that day on account of Christmas Celebration, therefore, we have preponed the event on this day. The event was an initiative by the students of the Department of Mathematics; Co-ordinated by Mrs. Nenzebi Ch Sangma, Assistant Professor, Department of Mathematics and Mr. Habul Chandra Das, Associate Professor & HoD, Department of Mathematics monitored the entire process.      

 Participant’s Profile: 

  A total of  200   students and almost all the faculty members from all the departments of Science Stream attended the programme.

 Description about the Program: 

  The inaugural function began by the Anchors  Ms. Sneha Paul and Ms. Sellorine N Sangma, 5th Semester Maths Major Students.  Ms. Nenzebi Ch Sangma, Assistant Professor, Department of Mathematics, who was the Convener of the Organising Committee, had welcomed the guests. The Principal, Rev. Fr. Januarius S Sangma, SDB had in his speech appreciated the department for organising such an august event and motivated the other departments too to organise such programmes in future. He exhorted the students to be ambassadors to young school students of perceiving mathematics positively, overcome phobia towards this subject, do group study of it coupled with personal practise at home. Mr. Habul Chandra Das, Associate Professor & HoD, Department of Mathematics, had emphasized on the need of celebration of such great personalities to inspire the students to walk in their footsteps.

   The following events were hosted in the daylong celebration:

 (i)  Group Seminars Contest were organised by 5th and 3rd Semester students    of the department of Mathematics in which the 5th Semester students lead by  Ms. Chenia N Marak came out as winners.

 (ii)  Quiz Contest among the 5 different Schools of the Town was conducted in which the students of Don Bosco Higher Secondary School, Tura came out as winners.

  At the end Judges had distributed the prizes to the participants.

 Feedback: 

   Many of the faculty members present in the programme expressed their gratitude to the staff of the Department of Mathematics for creating awareness among the students for taking active role in organising such events and praised the students for their Nobel initiatives. 

   Vote of thanks was proposed by Ms. Viska Viva Ch Marak , a 5th Semester Maths Major Student. The daylong programme was concluded with the National Anthem.

 Report Submitted by: 

 Mr. Habul Chandra Das , HoD &Associate professor

&

Ms. Nenzebi Ch Sangma, Convener & Assistant professor,

Department: Mathematics, Don Bosco College, Tura.
